stories.headline: Bridge collapse derails freight train in Russia's Arkhangelsk region
stories.summary: A span of a rail bridge over the Viled River collapsed early Tuesday, derailing freight cars and stranding at least eight long-distance passenger trains; no one was hurt and investigators are looking into the cause.

stories.summary: Jeremy Fears Jr. had 18 points and 11 assists and the Spartans led wire to wire at the United Center to improve to 3-0; Jordan Scott blocked a career-high six shots.

breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 501 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Nov. 10 close (mimics MMFI). Roughly unchanged from 69.3%, still just under the 70 line.

fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed held at 33 (fear), basically unchanged from Monday and a week ago, and well below 44 a month ago, so the rebound hasn't turned into real confidence.

markets.summary: Stocks slipped Tuesday after October CPI came in hotter than expected: headline prices rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, versus forecasts of 0.3% and 0.2%. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93, the Dow 0.30% to 52,231.89 and the Nasdaq 0.74% to 25,065.87, which put the Nasdaq back below its 40-week average. Small caps held up better, with the Russell 2000 off 0.68% at 2,821.38 and still just above its 40-week average. Rates jumped, with the 10-year Treasury yield up about nine basis points to roughly 4.99% after Fed Governor Waller said he leans toward a December hike and would consider a half-point move. Gold futures fell 2.05% to $4,030.20 and silver futures 2.78% to $51.10, both well below their 40-week averages. Nvidia fell 5.47% to $168.89 as the probe into CEO Jensen Huang widened, while breadth held near 69% and Fear & Greed stayed at 33.

stories.headline: Nvidia stock falls again in fallout from alleged CEO China spy affair
stories.summary: Shares dropped 5.47% after a 4% fall Monday; Trump said the FBI is investigating, and a shareholder class action was filed in San Jose. Dan Ives expects the board probe to take four to six weeks and weigh on the stock until then.

stories.headline: Alleged spy plot targeting CEO Jensen Huang raises questions about Nvidia's future
stories.summary: AP looks at reputational risk, the lack of a clear successor and new scrutiny from shareholders and lawmakers; Trump says Huang had no idea the woman was a spy.

stories.headline: SpaceX sets date for Starship Flight 15, plans first tower catch of the ship
stories.summary: SPCX rose 0.72% to $143.09, a three-day advance, after SpaceX announced the next Starship flight and its first planned ship catch.

stories.headline: Why is Space Exploration Technologies stock gaining today?
stories.summary: Investors are still reacting to NASA naming SpaceX one of eight CLPS-2 lunar providers and a 2028 Starship task order, while Stifel kept its Buy and $190 target.

stories.headline: SpaceX must face sex-bias claims after appeals court rejects arbitration request
stories.summary: The 9th Circuit let eight former engineers' lawsuit proceed in court rather than private arbitration; SpaceX denies the allegations.

stories.headline: Cameco excited, but cautious, about power demand from Big Tech
stories.summary: CEO Tim Gitzel said AI data-center demand is meaningful upside but not the foundation of the nuclear thesis. CCJ fell 3.32% to $72.87.

headlines.headline: Stocks fall after a hotter-than-expected inflation report
headlines.summary: The S&P 500 lost 0.4%, the Dow 0.3% and the Nasdaq 0.7% after October consumer prices rose more than economists forecast.

headlines.headline: US close: Stocks head south following hotter-than-expected CPI reading
headlines.summary: Treasury yields rose as Fed Governor Waller said further tightening is on the table, with the 10-year settling near 4.99%.

headlines.headline: Gold, silver plunge as hotter U.S. inflation raises prospect of larger Fed rate hike
headlines.summary: Spot gold fell about 2.6% to near $4,032 and silver about 3.6% to near $51.41 as yields and the dollar rose.

weather.summary: A strong cold front sweeps from the Midwest to the East Coast Wednesday and Thursday, with a few damaging-wind storms possible in the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys and the season's coldest air so far behind it, including first freezes for many areas and a hard freeze reaching into the South this weekend. A coastal low brings rain, wind and minor coastal flooding to the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast Thursday, while the West stays unseasonably warm with near-record highs possible in the Northwest and Great Basin.
